title: Microgrid Architect Lead, Power Generation
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

THE POWER GENERATION TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

- Build an islanded grid at gigawatt scale, from a blank sheet. Generation, storage and compute running with no utility behind them, where the machine you design is the only thing holding frequency. No playbook exists at this size, so the architecture you set becomes the reference.

- Get power online in months, not years. Interconnection queues are measured in years and we do not have them. Generating our own power is how a site goes from signed lease to live compute inside six months, and the power system is the long pole in that plan.

- Make one power block, then build it a thousand times. A repeatable block and cluster unit, validated once and stamped across the fleet, is the only route to the scale we are targeting. Every bespoke site is schedule we do not get back.

- Design a grid whose largest load answers back. Compute is not passive demand here. Load behaviour, curtailment and shedding are design variables you negotiate and specify, a lever almost no power system engineer has ever been handed.

ROLE SCOPE

- Own the system design basis for the islanded grid, fixing voltage levels, topology, grounding, redundancy boundaries and the repeatable block and cluster unit, with v1 and the site and block single-lines issued inside six months.

- Treat the block as a product rather than a project, holding one standard design across sites, driving out the variation that turns a repeatable build back into bespoke engineering, and freezing the design early enough that procurement and construction are never absorbing late change.

- Write the internal grid code that every generator, BESS, inverter, transformer and ITR must meet, own the conformance evidence that proves compliance before equipment ships rather than after it lands, and own the technical content of generation and electrical equipment specifications and the technical evaluation of bids, with v0.1 in vendors' hands before the first major RFP.

- Build the model of record yourself and own the study register, producing the first-pass generation, BESS and reserve sizing and the first load flow, short circuit and transient stability results, then accepting or rejecting every vendor and EPC study against it.

- Set the stability and protection philosophy, covering the loss-of-largest-unit contingency, reserve policy and a load shedding

THE ENERGY TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

- Put solar, storage and gas in the ground at an install rate no one in the construction market has hit. We are building generation across multiple gigawatt sites at once, on a schedule traditional EPC delivery cannot meet.

- Secure supply at a scale and timeline the supply chain cannot meet, and reshore it ourselves. Cells, containers, transformers and turbines are all constrained, so we qualify new suppliers and stand up domestic capacity instead of waiting in line.

- Make solar, gas and storage combine into power steady enough to run AI workloads. A training run does not tolerate a dip, so the hybrid plant has to behave like firm generation even when the resource behind it does not.

- Clear balancing authority certification, firm load rights, permits and interconnection against long clocks and a shifting policy environment. These approvals sit on the critical path to every gigawatt, so we work them years ahead of the build.

ROLE SCOPE

- Own the power conversion layer across storage and solar, PCS and inverter topology, DC architecture, filtering and the conversion interface to MV collection, as one standard repeated across concurrent gigawatt sites.

- Write the PCS and inverter specification vendors bid against, qualify platforms on measured behavior rather than datasheet, and hold OEM engineering to the spec through factory witness testing, site acceptance and warranty.

- Set the converter-level control requirements that let the plant hold firm load, grid-forming and grid-following operation, ride-through, step-load response and reactive capability, and hand a defensible interface to the storage, controls and protection leads.

- Lead conversion-side energization and commissioning in the field, through first charge and discharge, islanding and transfer tests, and step-load testing against real AI load profiles.

- Root-cause converter trips, derates and firmware regressions across the fleet, and fold every fix back into the standard design so the next site does not repeat it.

title: PhD Research Intern, Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research - 2027
description:
We are recruiting outstanding Research Interns to work on autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI! Intelligent machines that can perceive, reason, and safely interact with people and the physical world are rapidly becoming a reality. Self-driving cars, autonomous delivery and construction vehicles, mobile manipulators, and other robotic systems are moving closer to widespread deployment. However, fundamental research challenges remain before these systems can operate safely, reliably, and autonomously in complex, unfamiliar environments.
For example, how can we:

• Develop new training paradigms that use perception and interaction to train autonomous vehicle and robot policies in closed loop?

• Equip autonomous systems with online and offline assurances that meet the requirements of safety-critical applications?

• Enable vehicles and robots to navigate across new environments, tasks, and embodiments?

• Build systems that reason under uncertainty and interact safely and naturally with people and other agents?

These are some of the exciting questions being explored by NVIDIA ’s Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research (ASPIRE) group. Our diverse, interdisciplinary team conducts foundational research spanning foundation model design, embodied reasoning, safety, closed-loop training and evaluation, and agentic workflows for Physical AI development. We also investigate related areas including decision-making under uncertainty, deep learning, reinforcement learning, simulation, and the verification and validation of safety-critical AI systems. Our focus is on fundamental research, and lab members are encouraged to publish their work and open-source their code. NVIDIA is known for its collaborative culture, and our researchers work closely with experts across the company in autonomous vehicles, robotics, perception, simulation, and machine learning. This creates opportunities to influence real-world products while retaining the freedom and bandwidth to conduct groundbreaking, publishable research.
What you’ll be doing:

• Designing and implementing cutting-edge techniques for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI.

• Conducting original research and publishing your results.

• Collaborating with research colleagues, internal product teams, and external researchers.

• Transferring technology you’ve developed to relevant product groups.

What we need to see:

• Currently pursuing a PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

• Relevant research experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, or autonomous systems.

• Strong knowledge of the theory and practice of vehicle or robot autonomy-or expertise in a related area, with a strong interest in applying your work to autonomous systems.

• A track record of research excellence, demonstrated through publications at leading conferences and journals-such as RSS, ICRA, CoRL, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, TAC, etc.-and through other research artifacts such as open-source software.

• Exceptional Python programming skills; experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus.

• Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required, along with the ability to thrive in a dynamic, research-focused team.

Are you intellectually curious, collaborative, and motivated to solve complex problems at the intersection of AI and the physical world? If so, you may be a great fit for NVIDIA .

title: Head of Forward Engineering
description:
ABOUT HIYA

At Hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective.

Voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. When customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve.

Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes.

This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Scam and spoofed calls are one of the largest fraud problems in the world, and the place to stop them is inside the network. Hiya's Voice Intelligence Platform serves more than 500 million people in over 40 countries through mobile operators, device makers, and enterprises, deciding in real time which calls to flag, which to block, and which to deliver with a name and a reason attached. Every operator, device maker, and partner that adopts Hiya extends that to everyone they serve, and the engineers who make those adoptions happen are the ones you will lead.

Forward Engineering connects Hiya to the operators, device makers, enterprises, and partners who place and deliver calls. Solutions architects work with a customer from the first technical conversation, showing how Hiya fits and what it will take to launch. Forward deployed engineers integrate, launch, run, and grow each deployment. Our distribution platform gives them the gateways, SDKs, and tooling to bring on new customers quickly and consistently, adapting only where a customer's network requires it. We opened twelve new operator integrations last year; the aim is to do that at a scale and pace we have not reached before.

This is a founding leadership role, reporting to the CTO. You will inherit strong engineers in the United States and Europe, decide how the department is organized, and build it out as Hiya grows in North America, Europe, and Asia. The work comes down to understanding what each customer needs, getting them live quickly, and keeping their service reliable as we scale.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Lead and grow forward deployed engineering and solutions architecture across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific, and hire the people each market needs

- Own the distribution platform: hosted gateways for our APIs, SDKs for partner and device maker distribution, and the tooling that lets a forward deployed engineer adapt Hiya to a customer's network without forking the product

- Own the reliability and cost to serve of every live integration, and set the on-call and incident model that keeps them running

- Work with Product Engineering on a clear agreement for what Forward Engineering adapts for a customer and how customer needs reach the product roadmap

- Partner with Sales and Customer Success leadership across the full deal lifecycle, from technical pre-sales and solution design through launch, retention, and expansion, and share accountability for those outcomes

- Bring what customers and partners need back to the roadmap as patterns rather than one-off requests

- Hire, coach, and develop managers and senior engineers, and hold the bar on quality and customer trust across every region

- Set the department’s strategy and run its operating plan, including headcount, budget, and the metrics you report to the leadership team

- This is a hybrid role with 3 days per week in office in Seattle. Expect 30 to 40 percent travel to customers and partners

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

- You have 10+ years in customer-facing technical roles, with at least 4 le

title: Quality Engineer (SDET)
description:
About StarCompliance

StarCompliance is on a mission to make compliance simple and easy. Trusted globally by enterprise financial institutions, the user-friendly STAR platform empowers organizations to achieve regulatory compliance while safeguarding their integrity and business reputations. Through a customizable, 360-degree view of employee activity, the STAR software enables firms to automate the detection and resolution of potential areas of conflict while streamlining daily workflows and increasing efficiency.
Role
The Platform Quality Engineer is a hands-on engineering role within StarCompliance ’s centralised Platform Quality Engineering function, responsible for ensuring platform-level quality assurance across the enterprise SaaS platform.
Reporting to the Lead Quality Architect, the Platform Quality Engineer contributes directly to the design, implementation, and maintenance of automated quality controls that validate cross-service integration, core enterprise user journeys, and non-functional platform characteristics. The role is focused primarily on integration and API-level testing across a distributed, cloud-native system, including asynchronous and event-driven workflows.

StarCompliance ’s enterprise platform is built on distributed services and cloud infrastructure, including messaging and integration components such as Azure Service Bus. The Platform Quality Engineer is expected to understand how these systems behave under load, failure, and recovery conditions, and how to test them to ensure reliability, resilience, and performance at scale.
The role places strong emphasis on validating failure modes, resilience, and recovery behaviour across distributed services, diagnosing complex system failures using logs, telemetry, and test data, and contributing to enterprise performance testing.
The Platform Quality Engineer works closely with Product Owners and engineering teams to understand upcoming platform changes and integrations, ensuring the enterprise platform is validated under realistic functional and load scenarios ahead of release
Responsibilities

• Design, implement, and maintain automated tests primarily at the integration and API layers to validate behaviour across distributed services.

• Develop tests that validate asynchronous and event-driven workflows, including messaging, retries, ordering, and failure scenarios (e.g. Azure Service Bus-based integrations).

• Contribute production-quality code to shared automation frameworks and quality tooling used across the enterprise platform.

• Design and execute performance and scalability tests for the enterprise SaaS platform

• Build and maintain performance test data, scenarios, and workloads that reflect real-world usage patterns, including message throughput and concurrency.

• Integrate automated functional and performance tests into CI/CD pipelines, contributing to reliable, high-signal quality gates.

• Support validation activities within the Staging environment as the primary platform integration and quality assurance layer

• Analyse functional, integration, and performance test results to identify systemic platform risks and improvement opportunities.

• Partner with Product Owners to understand upcoming platform changes and integrations, preparing targeted integration and performance tests in advance.

• Collaborate with architecture, platform, and engineering teams to improve system testability, reliability, and observability.

• Apply AI-assisted engineering tools to accelerate test creation, improve coverage, analyse failures, and reduce test flakiness.

• Adhere to and contribute to quality standards, patterns, and engineering practices defined by the centralised Platform Quality Engineering function

Skills and Experience

• Demonstrable experience in platform- or enterprise-scale SaaS application quality assurance, with a focus on validating integration, non-functional characteristics, and release readiness across distributed systems.

title: Meridial – Scientist – In Vivo Neurophysiology
description:
About Meridial
 
Meridial is a Focused Research Organisation (FRO) with a mission to bring connectomics into the living brain. We are building a platform for longitudinal, synapse-resolution mapping of functional neural circuitry in preclinical models. Our aim is to deploy this platform for translational projects and improve drug development outcomes for disorders of the central nervous system. 
 
Meridial is a new not-for-profit FRO in the Convergent Research Ecosystem and funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA).
 
About the role
Meridial is seeking an experienced experimental neuroscientist to join our team as Scientist - In Vivo Neurophysiology.
This is a hands-on scientific role focused on developing and performing advanced in vivo experiments in mice that combine intracellular electrophysiology, two-photon imaging and optogenetic stimulation. You will develop new approaches as part of Meridial’s programme to create advanced 3D imaging and photostimulation technologies for functional mapping of neural circuits.
Your initial focus will be to establish electrophysiological ground-truth measurements for Meridial’s optical approaches to mapping functional neural connectivity. You will combine targeted intracellular recordings with optical imaging and stimulation to understand how synaptic activity and neuronal spiking are reflected in fluorescence signals. Your results will help guide experimental strategy and serve as a crucial foundation for interpreting our optical data. You will also contribute more broadly to Meridial’s experimental programme. That will include performing longitudinal two-photon imaging and optogenetic experiments and developing new approaches that extend the capabilities of our platform.
We are looking for an exceptional experimentalist who combines strong electrophysiological and imaging expertise with scientific independence. You will join a growing Experimental Team and report to the Director of Experimental Research. You will work closely with engineers and computational researchers across Meridial and help train and mentor experimental team members.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and do not make hiring or employment decisions on the basis of race, color, religion or religious belief, ethnic or national origin, nationality, sex, gender, gender-identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law or company policy. We strive for a diverse, healthy and safe workplace and strictly prohibit harassment of any kind.

We know human connections are what make teams strong, so we regularly do coffee chats, game-playing, story-telling, and more, to build strong relationships.
If you're entrepreneurial and seek an environment that values impact, ownership, and flexibility we look forward to meeting you!
The Opportunity
Dash is a managed AI teammate for small teams, built by Process Street . It picks up the recurring work that falls between people - the follow-ups, the handoffs, the things everyone assumes someone else did - and does it in Slack or Microsoft Teams, checking with a human before anything goes out.
Dash is new, and most of the people who'd love it haven't heard of it yet. Your job is to change that, and to turn the attention you create into pipeline.
This is demand creation, not demand capture, and the distinction shapes everything. There's no proven channel to scale, no playbook to inherit, and no installed base to build referral or expansion programs on. Every source of growth has to be invented and proven before anyone can optimize it.
The role has four connected parts: create attention, produce the content that sustains it, convert it into pipeline, and keep finding the next advantage. They're one job. The campaigns only work because there's a content engine behind them, the content only compounds because there's a conversion engine in front of it, and none of it holds for long without constant experimentation.
Dash runs like a startup inside a funded one. Process Street has investors behind it. Dash has a small team, its own budget, and has to earn its next dollar - which is exactly why this role exists. Budget won't be the lever that makes a campaign succeed. Creativity, timing, partnerships, and earned attention will be. We want someone whose instinct is to manufacture reach rather than purchase it, and who treats a small budget as a design constraint rather than an obstacle. The same discipline applies to the direct marketing engine: spend should be deliberate, measured, and defensible against the pipeline it produces.
You'll have real leverage behind you. Much of our content, research, and distribution runs on an automated production layer, so one person here can put far more into market than they could at a company doing this by hand. You won't be limited by how much you can produce. You'll be limited by what you decide is worth making - and whether it's good enough to ship, backed by a system that moves as fast as you think.
What You'll Do

title: Mechanical Engineer, Thermofluids
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

THE THERMOFLUIDS R&D TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

- Reject 10s of GW of heat, starting now. Fluidstack is targeting 10s of GW of compute over the next two years. Every watt of it becomes heat that has to go somewhere, and no cooling team has ever been asked to open at that scale rather than grow into it.

- Design and build the machines, because nobody can supply them. The merchant compressor market cannot deliver at this rate, and the vendor base behind today’s chillers will not scale to gigawatts. We are taking compressor and chiller design in house, working on machine architectures nobody sells today, and going from blank sheet to production faster than this industry thinks is possible.

- Own every thermofluids problem behind the fleet, not just the chiller. Working fluid and cycle architecture, heat exchangers at a scale that dominates the cost of the plant, two-phase heat transfer at the chip, and thermal energy storage. All of it is open, and whatever this team lands gets built thousands of times.

ROLE SCOPE

- Define what the machine has to be, owning the cycle model that sets the working fluid and the pressures, temperatures and flows the compressor, turbine and exchangers are designed against.

- Design heat exchangers with surface areas running into millions of square meters, among the largest single drivers of a data center’s physical footprint.

- Design the fluid system around the machine: piping, valves, headers, relief and isolation, sized against the pressure-drop budget the cycle can afford and the pressures the fluid actually runs at.

- Run the trades that decide the machine: air-side temperature rise, face velocity and subcooling. Derive the operating points from coupled exchanger ratings rather than asserted approach temperatures, so infeasible designs get caught in the model instead of in hardware.

- Take the cycle predictions onto the test stand and reconcile them against measured COP, then say plainly where the model was wrong.

title: Senior DevSecOps Engineer Contract
Software Engineer, Simulation
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Simulation Teams

Simulation is a mission-critical part of how we build Wayve's driving intelligence. It lets teams evaluate changes faster, investigate failures and build confidence in the driving stack before it reaches the road.

Wayve's end-to-end driving stack creates a distinctive simulation challenge. There are no intermediate stages where simulated signals can be injected, so simulation has to be end to end too: reproducing the behaviour of a learned driving system across sensor data, model inference, routing, control and vehicle dynamics. Our simulator needs to be realistic enough to give meaningful signal, reproducible enough for teams to trust the results, and descriptive enough to explain the differences between simulated and on-road behaviour.

You'll join the Core Simulation team. Our open-loop and closed-loop workflows share one codebase, with different components configured depending on the use case. You'll start with the team focused on high-scale open-loop evaluation, while contributing to shared components that also underpin GAIA-powered closed-loop simulation, where generative world models are integrated with the driving stack. Your role is to enable and productionise these capabilities, not primarily to train the models.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

- Work hands-on in our shared, modern C++ and Python simulation codebase

- Implement scoped features and integrate driving-stack components, simulated robot systems and new vehicle-platform capabilities

- Support and test different simulation configurations, with an initial focus on high-scale open-loop evaluation

- Investigate differences between on-road and simulated execution, tracing issues across component interfaces, data flows, timing and configuration

- Improve automated testing, observability, reproducibility, reliability and developer tooling

- Profile simulator workloads and contribute performance and scalability improvements

- Collaborate with Simulation, Robotics, Autonomy, Evaluation, Platform and Data teams to clarify requirements and resolve integration issues

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

- Developing and maintaining production-quality components in Wayve's simulation system using modern C++ and Python

- Integrating driving-stack components, simulated robot systems and new vehicle platforms into the shared simulation environment

- Making sure components interact correctly across the simulation workflows they support

- Finding the root cause of on-road vs. simulation differences across data, inference and simulated components

- Making simulation more reproducible, reliable and debuggable, and faster, so we can run ever larger evaluation workloads efficiently

- Contributing to technical designs and helping evolve the quality and maintainability of the codebase

 

🙌 You should apply if

- You have professional experience developing, delivering and maintaining production software in a collaborative engineering environment

- You have strong software development skills in C++ and Python, with depth in at least one and the ability to work effectively in the other (equal expertise in both isn't required)

- You have experience integrating and debugging components in a complex software system, reasoning across interfaces, data flows, timing and failure modes

- You have relevant experience in simulation (robotics or AV), ideally at the integration level, or in another complex systems domain with clearly transferable challenges

- You have experience integrating and working with ML components (e.g. PyTorch models, CUDA, QNN)

- You have strong software engineering fundamentals: testing, maintainability, code

title: FP&A Sr Specialist | Digital Assets
description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking an FP&A Senior Specialist to be the finance partner for our Digital Assets organization. Today that means our crypto trading and custody business in Brazil and the digital asset products inside Nu Global, including stablecoin balances, cross-border money movement, and crypto trading. As Nubank and the Digital Assets business expands to additional geographies, you will own the finance view of this business in each market it enters.

Digital Assets is both a customer product and a set of rails. Stablecoins, FX, on and off ramps, and card spending can be a source of revenue, a cost to manage, or the reason a customer chooses us in the first place. This role is about building as the business grows, including how we model and forecast it, starting with the economics of a single customer, trade, or balance and building up to the business P&L. You will also own the position Finance takes on those numbers with Digital Assets leadership.

The scope covers every digital asset product we offer, in every market where we offer it. Economics and accounting differ by product, entity, and country, and many of the answers are still being worked out. You will decide which assumptions matter most, make them explicit, and revise them as the business learns.

You will operate with a high degree of autonomy and regular exposure to the leaders who run these businesses. You will be expected to hold a position when the analysis supports it, push back with evidence, and take direct feedback. This is a senior individual contributor role. You will stay hands-on in the models and analysis, and you will help raise the standard of work across the FP&A team around you.

YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

- Own the planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting cycles for Digital Assets across Brazil and Nu Global, with accountability for the integrity of the numbers and for the position Finance takes on them with leadership.

- Build the P&L for each digital asset product, from trading and swaps to custody and stablecoin yield, and model how volume, take rate, balances, pricing, and partner costs flow through to Nubank's consolidated results.

- Track gross profit and cost-to-serve, including execution and liquidity costs, custody and platform provider fees, payment network and funding costs, and regulatory and audit requirements, and bring a point of view on what should change when results move.

- Support expansion into new geographies with the financial analysis behind each launch, including unit economics, local rails and funding methods, and the effect of licensing and legal entity structures.

- Partner with Controllership, Treasury, Legal, and Risk on custody accounting, reconciliation, yield accrual, and liquidity planning as assets under custody and stablecoin balances scale.

- Work with Digital Assets product and business leaders early enough to shape pricing, product, and investment decisions.

- Prepare clear, concise executive materials that simplify complex topics, often on short timelines.

- Use AI, advanced analytics, and automation to speed up planning and analysis, while keeping the judgment to review and challenge AI-generated output.

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

Required

- You can build the P&L for a trading, custody, payments, or banking product from a blank page, understand how the lines interact, and find what is wrong in a model built by someone else or by an AI tool.

Location: Fully remote, worldwide

title: Machine Learning Compiler Engineer
description:
About the position

We’re looking for compiler engineers to join a new ML Compilers Team at Jane Street. 

Machine learning is a critical pillar of our global business. Our ever-evolving trading environment serves as a unique, rapid-feedback platform for ML experimentation, allowing us to incorporate new ideas with relatively little friction. Our ML team is full of people with a shared love for the craft of software engineering, and for designing APIs and systems that are delightful to use.

ML compilers let us quickly turn research ideas and novel architectures into high-throughput training jobs and low-latency inference. To get the most out of our hardware resources and enable rapid model development and deployment, we are working to understand and improve the current ML compiler technologies and explore where it makes sense to build our own solutions. In this role, you would shape the development of our compiler stack.

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in.

About you

The ideal candidate has worked on an ML compiler in the past, but non-ML compiler experience is also valuable. Experience with any part of the stack is fine, be it high-level ML frameworks (PyTorch, Jax, TensorFlow), graph compilers (Inductor, XLA, TVM) or kernel DSLs (Triton, Helion, cuTile). You should understand how all those pieces fit together even if you are unfamiliar with specific parts. 

Some other things you might be excited about are:

• Optimisations in ML compilers: algebraic rewriting, materialise vs recompute tradeoffs and fusion, equality saturation, scheduling languages, loop-level optimisation

title: Staff Product Manager - Agent Trust
description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

About the Team
The Fraud team is building the largest network of trusted identities in the US. We help customers onboard legitimate users and stop bad actors before they cause downstream harm. Our products span the risk lifecycle: Identity Verification and Monitor for onboarding and compliance, and Protect, our fraud intelligence platform.

 

We are extending that network to AI agents. Agents are starting to open accounts, link accounts, move money, and transfer between wallets for consumers. The protocols forming around them standardize how an agent identifies itself and what it may do, and leave the question of whether to trust it to the business on the receiving end. Agent Trust, our Know Your Agent (KYA) product, answers it, on top of the identity, consent, and risk infrastructure Plaid already runs.

 

You will take over Agent Trust: the decision on whether an action an AI agent takes on a financial account can be trusted. You will define how Plaid identifies agents, verifies the people behind them, and evaluates what they are authorized to do, and how that connects to portable identity, reusable KYC, and consumer permissions. You will sell that decision to financial institutions and to Plaid customers, and you will carry Plaid’s requirements into the standards bodies shaping this space, with the fraud engineering and data teams behind you.

 

Responsibilities:

- Own the vision, strategy, roadmap, and OKRs for Agent Trust. Decide what Plaid offers, to whom, and how it is packaged and priced.

- Define how Plaid identifies agents, verifies the humans behind them, and evaluates what they are allowed to do, for new accounts and existing ones.

- Connect Agent Trust to portable identity, reusable KYC, and consumer permission management, with the product teams that own those surfaces.

- Work directly with financial institutions and Plaid customers as the product expert: discovery, design partnerships, and GTM enablement.

- Represent Plaid’s product requirements in the industry groups and protocol working groups writing the specs for agent identity and authorization, with Partnerships and Legal.

- Partner with data science and engineering on what the product needs: signals, labels, success metrics, and the requirements that tie them together.

 

Qualifications:

- 8+ years of product management or equivalent product ownership, with meaningful time in fraud, identity, authentication, or payments risk

- Hands-on depth in identity and authorization protocols (OAuth 2.x and OIDC, FIDO and WebAuthn, FDX or Open Banking consent), or in bot, device, and agent detection systems

- Track record of growing a new product line, from early design partners and first customers to repeatable sales

- Experience building with and selling to enterprise customers or financial institutions

- Clear writing, and the ability to translate between protocol engineers, data scientists, GTM, and executives

Nice to have:

- Direct work on agentic protocols or programs (MCP, A2A, AP2, ACP, UCP, Visa TAP, Mastercard Agentic Tokens, Verifiable Intent)

- Standards-body participation (FDX, FIDO Alliance, OpenID Foundation, Linux Foundation, W3C)

- KYC, reusable

title: First Line Manager
description:
We're building a sales team that wins, and we're looking for the leaders who'll make it happen.

As a First Line Manager at Lio, you're a true player-coach. You build, coach and lead a team of 6-8 Account Executives, and when a big deal is on the line, you're right there in the room helping close it. You don't chase a quota of your own. You own your team's number, and the goal is ambitious: hit the target together, then double it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Lead your team to its number. You help your team hit its target and build the pipeline and habits that let it grow from there.

- Be there when deals need you. You join calls, visit customers on site and help close seven-figure opportunities. When the usual playbook isn't enough, you get creative.

- Know what's real in your forecast. You're curious about every deal and look into it yourself, so you and your team always know where you stand.

- Take ownership. If a deal stalls, you reach out to the champion yourself. If it needs a workshop, you're happy to run it. You do what the deal needs.

- Help your reps grow. You make coaching, training and deal reviews part of the team's week, and nothing motivates you more than seeing your AEs succeed.

- Bring our way of selling to life. You know the product well and sell in an inquisitive, consultative and educative way, so your team learns it from you.

WHO YOU ARE

- You've carried a quota, closed complex B2B or enterprise deals, and still enjoy selling.

- You've led a sales team, had a first management experience, or feel ready to take that step. Many of our future managers start as AEs at Lio, get to know how we sell, and then grow into leadership.

- You're entrepreneurial and find creative ways to reach a goal.

- You like to check things for yourself and ask good questions, including of your own team.

- You love learning and are excited to adapt to how we sell rather than bringing a ready-made playbook.

- Building a team excites you more than your own quota.

THIS MIGHT NOT BE THE RIGHT FIT IF…

- you'd prefer to focus purely on people management and step away from deals.

- you'd rather stick to one proven playbook than adapt it.

- you'd rather keep your own quota than build a team.

- you prefer to rely on your team's forecast without digging into it.

WHY NOW

Our Go-To-Market team will grow significantly over the next year. You'd join early enough to shape how we lead sales, at a point where you can already see it working. Together with our sales leadership, you'll build your team and help define what great sales management looks like at Lio.

If you're hungry to build a team that outperforms every target, to turn good reps into great ones, and to win the biggest deals together, we want to hear from you.

Overview

Certara accelerates the potential of bringing medicines to market and to patients using biosimulation software, technology, and services to transform traditional drug discovery and development. Our clients include more than 2,400 biopharmaceutical companies, academic institutions, and regulatory agencies across 70 countries.
Our goal is to enable the life sciences industry’s use of data, modeling, and analytics to make better decisions across the various phases of discovery and drug development. Our software and scientists incorporate modern advances in scientific understanding, drug development experience, data analysis, and AI resulting in significant opportunities to decrease the cost and increase the probability of success for new drug approval and commercialization.
The R&D Partner is a senior individual contributor who sells large, complex, multi-year deals that bring together Certara ’s software and services across the full drug development lifecycle, from discovery through regulatory approval and market access. These deals are not single-product sales. They combine capabilities from several Certara portfolios into one integrated solution for pharmaceutical and biotech customers, and they may involve partners within Certara ’s ecosystem. [Confirm ecosystem scope, e.g., alliance, channel, and partner-involved deals.]

Responsibilities

• Forecast and report: Keep CRM records current, provide accurate forecasts, and take part in pipeline and business reviews.
• Share market insight: Bring customer and market feedback on integrated-R&D buying trends back into commercial strategy.

Success Measures

• Attainment of individual bookings quota on integrated, multi-portfolio deals.
• Qualified pipeline and win rate on large integrated opportunities.

• Deal quality: margin, contract term, and successful handoff to delivery.

• Forecast accuracy and CRM discipline.

• Feedback from customers and internal account teams on coordination and value delivered.

• 12+ years of enterprise sales, business development, or account leadership experience selling complex software and/or scientific or consulting services to pharmaceutical or biotech companies.
